summary: Test coverage is solid. All 16 TDD anchor tests are present and structurally sound. Core integration paths exercise production code, not hand-crafted stubs. Two findings: one minor gap (visibility_threads_through_to_storage bypasses the dispatcher gate and the AC14 variant is not reached for private visibility on the end-to-end path), one weak assertion (consume_succeeds_for_matching_args allows any non-32095 error to pass including a 500). Notes attached; no blocking findings.
methodology_applied: test-master (pyramid review: smoke → unit → integration → E2E)

pyramid_balance.unit: Good. Six unit tests in confirmation_token.rs::tests cover HMAC process scope, mint/consume roundtrip, cross-owner rejection, cross-content-hash rejection, TTL eviction, and concurrent atomic remove. No mocks — real DashMap + real HMAC.
pyramid_balance.integration: Good. 28 integration tests across four new files use the real axum router + real middleware + real SqliteStore through TestServer. No over-mocking observed.
pyramid_balance.e2e: None added in this task — expected per tech-spec (E2E lives in Task 5/AC3 netns test). Acceptable.

tdd_anchors_checklist.note: Asserts -32602, data.field=visibility, data.received=public, and row count=0. Tight.
visibility_threads_through_to_storage exists but drives sign_memory directly, bypassing dispatcher gate. See Finding F1.
Seeds 1 private + 1 public, asserts len==1 and attestation_id==public-id and visibility==public. Correct.
Asserts confirmation_token is_string, jti is_string, expires_at is_number. Adequate.
Asserts NOT -32095 and ledger.len()==0. See Finding F2 — weak success assertion.
Asserts -32095. Decision 5b cross-owner replay covered. Correct.

The task spec calls for tokio::time::pause+advance to test TTL expiry via sign_memory. The unit test evict_expired_removes_only_expired_rows tests the ledger eviction but NOT the consume-expired path via the dispatcher. consume() checks now < entry.expires_at; a token minted with TTL=Duration::ZERO will have expires_at <= now at consume time, so consume returns Invalid. This should be a test in confirmation_gate.rs driving sign_memory. NOT present as an integration test.
atomic_remove_if_under_concurrent_access: 16 tokio tasks, Barrier, exactly 1 wins. Correct.
Two ledger instances; cross-ledger consume fails. Correct.
TTL=0, 100 entries, evict_expired called synchronously, asserts 100 removed and len==0. Correct.

5 rows covered in Task 4 via production paths (InvalidParams-visibility, InvalidParams-allow_fallback, UnsupportedMode, PublicWriteRequiresConfirmation, EmbedderInvalid). 7 deferred rows are covered by the typed-helper pin test (catalogue_typed_helpers_pin_data_shapes) which verifies helper-level shapes, NOT production code paths. Per spec: 'A row is considered covered ONLY if the test induces the condition this way, not by hand-crafting a response.' The helper-level test does not satisfy the spec criterion for those 7 rows. However, per the spec's explicit design those rows are owned by Tasks 5/6 — this is documented and intentional. Acceptable for Task 4.

findings.title: visibility_threads_through_to_storage bypasses the dispatcher gate — the AC14 private-visibility end-to-end path is not exercised through the HTTP boundary
findings.detail: visibility_threads_through_to_storage calls tools::sign_memory() directly (bypassing handle_tool_call and resolve_visibility). This correctly exercises that the visibility arg reaches save_attestation and that the response envelope contains 'visibility': 'private'. However: (1) the TDD anchor name in the task spec is 'visibility_persisted_on_participate_public' and the test uses mode=local + Visibility::Private — not participate+public. The participate+public persistence path (which requires a confirmation token) is not proven to persist a public row in the DB. (2) The comment in the test acknowledges this limitation ('Asserting visibility persistence end-to-end here would require an arlocal mock... out of scope for Task 4'). This is a reasonable pragmatic scoping decision. Recommend adding one line to the existing test's assertion: also asserting that with mode=participate + visibility=public (via direct sign_memory on STORAGE_MODE=local which uses synthetic tx IDs) the DB row has visibility='public'. The confirmation gate lives in handle_tool_call, not in sign_memory, so direct-call tests can set any Visibility without a ceremony token.
findings.recommended_fix: In visibility_threads_through_to_storage, after the existing private assertion, add a second sign_memory direct call with Visibility::Public and assert the DB row visibility='public'. This requires no confirmation ceremony because it bypasses handle_tool_call.

findings.title: consume_succeeds_for_matching_args has a weak positive-path assertion — any non-32095 error (including 500) is treated as success
findings.detail: The test asserts: if let Some(e) = err { assert_ne!(code, -32095, ...) }. This means an internal server error (-32603), Arweave write failure, or any other error code is also treated as a 'pass'. The consumption of the ledger entry (ledger.len()==0) is the stronger proof that the gate was passed, but the test still allows any downstream failure to mask the pass. The assertion is correct for the specific finding (the gate did not reject) but gives a false success impression.
findings.recommended_fix: After asserting NOT -32095, also assert that ledger.len()==0 (already done, which is the real proof). Optionally add a comment: '// ledger.len()==0 is the definitive proof the gate passed; code may be non-200 due to Arweave failure at localhost:0'. This is documentation rather than a code fix but improves readability.

findings.title: consume_expired_rejected anchor test is missing as an integration test
findings.detail: The task spec TDD anchor list includes: 'confirmation_gate.rs::consume_expired_rejected — mint, advance test clock past expires_at via tokio::time::pause+advance, attempt sign. -32095.' This test is not present in the diff. The unit test evict_expired_removes_only_expired_rows covers the eviction loop removing expired rows but does NOT test that consume() returns Invalid for an expired entry that has NOT yet been evicted. The consume() predicate checks now < entry.expires_at — an expired-but-not-evicted entry will be rejected by consume but the entry stays in the DashMap (predicate returns false, remove_if removes nothing). The missing test would cover: mint with TTL=1ns → consume immediately → -32095.
findings.recommended_fix: Add confirmation_gate.rs::consume_expired_rejected: mint a token via ledger.mint() with TTL effectively zero (ConfirmationLedger::with_config(Duration::ZERO, ...) sets expires_at to now or slightly past), then attempt sign_memory → assert -32095. No tokio::time needed since SystemTime::now() > expires_at immediately for TTL=0.

findings.title: is_string_or_value always returns true — misleading field matcher name
findings.detail: In error_catalogue.rs: fn is_string_or_value(v: &Value) -> bool { !v.is_null() || v.is_null() } — this is a tautology (always true). The function is used to check the 'received' field. A non-null check (!v.is_null()) would be more meaningful since 'received' should echo the verbatim input. The current implementation accepts null, which shouldn't happen for a rejection based on a provided value.
findings.recommended_fix: Change to fn is_string_or_value(v: &Value) -> bool { !v.is_null() } or rename to fn is_any_value(_: &Value) -> bool { true } to make intent clear.

findings.title: anonymous_recall: owner_pubkey predicate behavior for anonymous callers is load-bearing but not directly tested
findings.detail: The comment in tools.rs (line ~1174 in the diff) notes: 'The owner_pubkey is the local server keypair on the anonymous path (the dispatcher's fallback)...the visibility-public predicate is the real gating filter.' The test seeds rows under server.server_pubkey() which happens to be the same fallback. If the fallback ever changes, the test would silently start seeding under a different owner than the dispatcher uses, and anonymous recall would return 0 rows (passing the wrong assertion). The test relies on server_pubkey() == fallback_pubkey() without asserting that invariant.
findings.recommended_fix: Add a comment in the test: '// rows are seeded under server_pubkey() because the dispatcher falls back to the server keypair pubkey for anonymous callers — these must match.' Or expose a test helper that returns the anonymous-path owner_pubkey explicitly.

positive_observations: ConfirmationLedger unit tests are self-contained with no mocks — real DashMap, real HMAC, real SystemTime. This is the right choice.

cross_owner_consume_rejected correctly verifies that the entry is NOT removed on owner mismatch (owner-A retry still succeeds). This correctly captures the DashMap::remove_if predicate-false behavior.
recall_owner_isolation.rs update correctly implements the AC13 forward-flag resolution: asserts HTTP 200, asserts zero rows (private writes don't surface), explains why.
visibility_rejected_on_local_writes_even_for_private_value covers the important edge case that the rejection is on field presence, not value.
visibility_rejected_for_non_canonical_value is table-driven across 5 bad inputs including whitespace-prefixed and empty string. Good boundary coverage.
The FailingEmbedder fixture correctly implements the task spec: fail_on_call=1 default means the first embed() call returns Vec::new(), triggering the production code path in sign_memory_inline.

catalogue_typed_helpers_pin_data_shapes verifies all 11 helper constructors and their error codes + kind discriminators in a single fast synchronous test. Good as a safety net for the deferred task rows.
Test file header comments accurately reference the decision numbers and AC citations.

test_independence.notes: Each test builds its own TestServer (in-memory SQLite). No shared global state observed. Seed functions take a TestServer reference and operate on its store. The concurrent race test uses Arc<ConfirmationLedger> correctly.

trigger_fidelity.notes: All 5 in-scope catalogue rows are triggered via production code paths: dispatcher boundary for InvalidParams, envelope check for UnsupportedMode, real DashMap ledger for PublicWriteRequiresConfirmation, FailingEmbedder via sign_memory() for EmbedderInvalid. No hand-crafted responses.
